newsitem.title: USA: Digital Q1 off to slow start - Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Digital Q1 off to slow start - Morgan.

text.p: Morgan Stanley analyst Steve Milunovich said that Digital Equipment Corp's first fiscal quarter is off to a slow start, and that the probability of a loss has increased, he said in a note to clients.

Milunovich said that after a visit with Digital senior management on Monday, they indicated that orders have been below plan through last week and Europe continues to be soft, with the U.S. and Far East a bit slower.
"Fiscal Q1 is off to a slow start, likely due to short term disruption from sales force changes," Milunovich said in a report. Digital shares were off 1/2 to 36-7/8.

Milunovich also said that server strength is offset by weakness in PCs, workstations and networking. "Consequently, a loss appears increasingly likely, we forecast red ink of $0.08 (EPS) on revenue of $3.31 billion," he said.
Milunovich also said that at next week's analyst meeting in New York, he expects Digital to target a net margin of seven percent by the fourth quarter of fiscal 1998.

"We are encouraged by the direction to be outlined next week and the potential earnings power of $6.00-$7.00 per share," Milunovich said, adding that given near-term earnings weakness, he would only be a buyer under $35 a share.
